name: Goldilocks funding regime: long only while 30-day funding is positive but not euphoric
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode. m = mean of fd(k) for k in i-n+1..i (skip nulls; need >=n/2 values). Long (1) iff lo < m <= hi AND close[i] > sma(close,100). Else 0. Position re-evaluated every bar (held while condition true).
rationale: Mildly positive funding signals sustained spot-led demand; above 0.05%/8h (~55%/yr) leverage is euphoric and prone to flush, negative funding marks bear regimes. Tests whether the middle band is where trend persists.
source: Binance funding docs; Coinglass funding-rate heatmap conventions; Kaiko 2022 'Funding rates as a positioning gauge'

name: Negative funding percentile dip inside an uptrend (shorts pay while trend intact)
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode, holdBars=10. Maintain ring of last pctWin fd values. Trigger on bar i if fd(i) is below the 10th percentile of the ring (ring full) AND close[i] > sma(close,200). Enter long for exactly 10 bars; no re-entry while held.
rationale: When funding is at its own yearly low while price sits above the 200-day average, shorts are crowded against the trend and pay to stay; a squeeze or simple carry drift favours longs.
source: Franz & Valentin 2020 'Crypto Covered Interest Parity' (funding as positioning); Cheng 2023 'Funding rates and return predictability' SSRN

name: Funding persistence: sustained premium streak as trend confirmation
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode. up = count of consecutive bars ending at i with fd(k) > base; down = consecutive bars with fd(k) <= base. Enter long when up >= streak. Exit (0) when down >= exitDays. Otherwise keep prior position.
rationale: A premium that persists above the 0.01% clamp for a week signals steady demand for long exposure; funding momentum, unlike a one-off spike, has been slow to mean-revert.
source: Binance funding clamp mechanics; practitioner 'funding streak' dashboards (Velo, Coinalyze)

name: Single extreme funding print fade (both sides)
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. On bar i: if fd(i) >= th -> -1 (short 3 bars); if fd(i) <= -th -> +1 (long 3 bars); else 0. No new entry while held.
rationale: A 0.1%/8h print (~110%/yr) is ten times the clamp and only occurs when one side is forced; such prints mark local extremes that unwind over days.
source: Coinglass liquidation/funding extremes; Deribit Insights 'funding spikes and local tops' 2021

name: Carry-adjusted momentum: 28-day return net of cumulative funding paid
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode. r = close[i]/close[i-lb]-1. c = sum over k in i-lb+1..i of fd(k)*settlementsPerDay (approximate cumulative funding a long paid). Long iff r - c > 0 AND c < 0.05; else 0.
rationale: A perp long's realised P&L is spot return minus funding; momentum that survives the carry drag reflects buyers who kept paying, while trend that only exists before funding is leverage-fuelled.
source: Moskowitz-Ooi-Pedersen 2012 time-series momentum; Koijen et al 2018 'Carry' (carry-adjusted returns)

name: Funding z-score reversion gated to low realised volatility
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. z = (fd(i) - mean(fd over zWin)) / std(fd over zWin). rv = rollingStd('ret',volWin). lowVol = rv below the volPct quantile of its own last volHist values. If lowVol and z >= 1.5 -> -1; if lowVol and z <= -1.5 -> +1; else 0.
rationale: In quiet markets funding extremes are positioning noise rather than information about a trend, so they revert; in volatile markets the same extremes often precede continuation.
source: Cheng 2023 SSRN 'Funding rates and return predictability'; practitioner 'quiet-market funding fade'

name: Funding-price divergence: rally that shorts keep fighting
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode, holdBars=7. On bar i: r = close[i]/close[i-lb]-1; fm = mean fd over k in i-lb+1..i. Enter long iff r >= minRet AND fm < 0. No re-entry while held.
rationale: Price up 10% in two weeks while average funding is negative means the rally was spot-driven and shorts are underwater; forced covering extends such moves.
source: Deribit Insights 2021 'Spot-led vs futures-led rallies'; Glassnode 'funding negative during uptrend' notes

name: Funding pinned at the clamp = no leverage interest, trade the ensuing 20-day breakout
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode, holdBars=10. frac = share of the last win bars where |fd(k) - pinned| <= tol. If frac >= minFrac and close[i] > donchian(20,i-1).upper -> long 10 bars. Else 0.
rationale: Funding resting exactly at Binance's 0.01% default for most of a month means the perp is dormant; the first breakout from such a dormant state tends to draw in fresh leverage and run.
source: Binance funding default clamp; Crabel-style compression logic applied to positioning

name: Funding slope: 7-day mean crossing above 30-day mean from below zero
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode. f7 = mean fd over last 7 bars, f30 = mean over last 30. Enter long when f7 crosses above f30 (f7>f30 now, f7<=f30 at i-1) AND f30 < 0.0001. Exit to 0 when f7 crosses below f30. Hold otherwise.
rationale: Rising funding from a depressed base indicates demand for long exposure returning before price confirms, a positioning-flow analogue of a moving-average cross.
source: Coinalyze/Velo funding moving-average dashboards; Gerritsen et al 2020 on technical rules in Bitcoin

name: Trend with a funding budget exit: leave once cumulative funding paid since entry exceeds 2%
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). Signal mode. Enter long when close[i] > sma(close,50) and not in cooldown; set ctx.state.paid=0. While long: paid += fd(i)*settlementsPerDay. Exit to 0 if close[i] < sma50 OR paid >= budget; a budget exit starts a cooldown of 10 bars before re-entry.
rationale: A trend is only worth holding on leverage while the cumulative carry stays small; once holders have paid 2% in funding the position is crowded and the trend is typically late.
source: Practitioner carry-budget rule (Jump Trading Research blog 2022 'The cost of being long');  r24b funding-exit result as prior

name: Open-interest trough inside a price uptrend (deleveraged trend has room)
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k) latest hourly OI snapshot known at close of bar k (null -> 0). Signal mode, holdBars=15. Keep ring of last oiWin oi values. Enter long when oi(i) <= min(ring) (new 90-day OI low) AND close[i] > sma(close,100). No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.] [prereg fix: oiWin 90 -> 60 (coin-OI 90-day lows inside an uptrend too rare on ~3 years of OI); ring must hold oiWin non-null values before any trigger.]
rationale: Leverage has been fully washed out while price still holds its trend, so there is no overhang of trapped longs to sell into strength; the next move up starts from a clean positioning base.
source: Glassnode 'OI reset' notes 2022; Coinglass OI research

name: OI-confirmed hourly impulse continuation
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=12. r1 = close[i]/close[i-1]-1; d = oi(i)/oi(i-1)-1. If r1 >= ret and d >= oiJump -> +1 (new longs opened the move); if r1 <= -ret and d >= oiJump -> -1 (new shorts opened it). Else 0. No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: A 1.5% hourly bar with OI rising 2% means new positions, not covering, drove the move; initiative flow with fresh leverage has tended to continue for several hours.
source: Binance OI metrics; Bessembinder & Seguin 1993 (OI and volume as price-move informativeness)

name: Short-squeeze exhaustion: price up on falling OI, fade it
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=12. r = close[i]/close[i-win]-1; d = oi(i)/oi(i-win)-1. If r >= ret and d <= oiDrop -> -1 (short 12 bars). Else 0. No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: Price rising while OI falls is short covering, which supplies no new buyers once the shorts are gone; such moves have tended to retrace.
source: Classic OI/price interpretation (Murphy 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets' ch.7) applied to perps

name: Joint 30-day high in price and open interest, exit on 10% OI drawdown
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). Signal mode. Enter long when close[i] = max(close over i-win+1..i) AND oi(i) = max(oi over i-win+1..i). While long track oiPeak = max oi since entry; exit (0) when oi(i) < oiPeak*(1-oiDd). Re-entry needs a fresh joint high. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: New price highs confirmed by new positioning highs mean fresh longs are funding the move; a 10% drop in OI is the earliest sign that those longs are leaving.
source: Murphy ch.7 OI confirmation; CME 'Open interest as trend confirmation' education pages

name: Shorts building into negative funding: squeeze setup
rule: fd(k)=ctx.fundingRate(k) = latest settled 8h funding known at close of bar k (null before 2020 -> return 0). oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). Signal mode, holdBars=7. fm = mean fd over last 3 bars; d = oi(i)/oi(i-7)-1. Enter long iff fm < 0 AND d >= oiUp. No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: Rising OI while funding is negative means shorts are the ones adding leverage; they are paying carry and are exposed to a squeeze, the mirror of the tested long-stall short.
source: Coinglass 'OI up + funding negative' playbook; mirror of s29-h-oi-funding-stall

name: Weekend OI build on a flat price, fade on Monday
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun). Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=2. On a bar with dow==0 (Sunday bar, closes Monday 00:00 UTC) find the last bar j with dow==5 (Friday). If oi(i)/oi(j)-1 >= oiUp AND |close[i]/close[j]-1| <= flat -> -1 (short 2 bars). Else 0. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: Weekend leverage is added by retail while market makers and institutions are offline; OI growing 5% over a flat weekend is positioning without conviction and has been unwound in the Monday session.
source: Kaiko weekend liquidity research 2023; Coinglass weekend OI notes

name: Weekend range breakout in the Monday-Tuesday session
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort. At the first bar with dow==1 and hour==0 (Monday 00:00) record wkHigh/wkLow = max high / min low over all bars with dow in {6,0} since the preceding Friday 23:00 bar, mid=(wkHigh+wkLow)/2. Through Monday and Tuesday bars (dow 1-2): if flat and close[i] > wkHigh -> +1; if flat and close[i] < wkLow -> -1. Exit when close crosses back through mid, or at the Tuesday bar with hour==exitHour. Flat otherwise, one trade per week.
rationale: Weekend bars are thin and define a consolidation; the first weekday session, when institutional and CME flow returns, resolves that range and the resolution has tended to carry.
source: Kaiko weekend liquidity research 2023; opening-range breakout logic (Crabel 1990) on the week

name: CME-gap fill: trade back toward the Friday 21:00 UTC close
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort. Store fri = close of the bar with dow==5 and hour==friHour. At the bar with dow==1 and hour==monHour: gap = close[i]/fri-1. If gap >= minGap -> -1 (short, target fri); if gap <= -minGap -> +1 (long, target fri). Exit when a bar's low<=fri (short) / high>=fri (long) is observed on a completed bar, i.e. set 0 at the first bar whose range touches fri, or after maxHold bars.
rationale: CME Bitcoin futures stop trading over the weekend, so any weekend move in spot shows as a gap on the CME chart; traders widely expect these gaps to fill, and if they do the expectation is self-reinforcing.
source: CME BTC futures contract specs; Arcane Research 2020 'Do CME gaps fill?' ; widely-asked retail rule

name: Weekend move reversal on Monday-Wednesday
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. On the bar with dow==0 (Sunday bar, closes Monday 00:00): find last bar j with dow==5 (Friday). w = close[i]/close[j]-1. If w >= minMove -> -1; if w <= -minMove -> +1; else 0.
rationale: Weekend moves happen on a fraction of weekday volume and without the arbitrage desks that anchor price to CME and spot ETFs; such thin-liquidity moves have reverted once the week opens.
source: Kaiko weekend volume studies; Baur et al 2019 'Bitcoin: weekend effect' (Finance Research Letters)

name: US equity-open hour momentum in crypto
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. On weekday bars (dow 1-5) with hour==openHour (the 13:00-14:00 UTC bar containing the 13:30 US cash open): r=close[i]/open[i]-1. If r >= minRet -> +1; if r <= -minRet -> -1; else 0.
rationale: Since 2020 crypto trades as a high-beta risk asset; the direction set in the hour of the US equity open reflects the day's risk flow and has carried into the early US session.
source: Hoang & Baur 2021 'How stable are stablecoins? / crypto-equity intraday correlation'; practitioner 'NYSE open' rule

name: Trend held weekdays only: flat over the weekend
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode. Trend = ema(close,20) > ema(close,100). Position = 1 iff trend AND the bar is not in the weekend window; weekend window = from the Friday bar with hour>=exitHour through the Sunday bar with hour 23 (i.e. dow==5 and hour>=20, dow in {6,0}). Else 0.
rationale: Answers 'should I hold over the weekend': weekend bars carry the gap/liquidation risk with little trend information, so a trend follower may keep the weekday drift and drop weekend variance.
source: Baur et al 2019 weekend effect; Kaiko weekend liquidity

name: Post-monthly-options-expiry breakout window
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, holdBars=5. expiry = last Friday of each UTC month (dow==5 and the bar's day-of-month + 7 > days in that month). In the daysAfter bars after an expiry bar: if close[i] > donchian(20,i-1).upper -> long 5 bars. Else 0.
rationale: Deribit monthly expiries concentrate dealer gamma; pinning suppresses moves into expiry and the hedging supply disappears afterward, so breakouts in the following days face less resistance.
source: Deribit Insights 'gamma and max pain' 2021-2023; SqueezeMetrics dealer-gamma framework

name: Post-quarterly-futures-expiry long
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, holdBars=10. Quarterly expiry = last Friday (dow==5) of March, June, September, December (UTC month from time). Enter long on the expiry bar's close for 10 bars.
rationale: Quarterly contract roll unwinds basis trades and futures-hedged inventory; after the roll the forced selling pressure is gone and crypto has tended to drift up in the following fortnight.
source: Binance/OKX/Deribit quarterly expiry calendars; CME roll literature (Mou 2010 'Limits to arbitrage and commodity index rolls')

name: Weekend-to-weekday volume ratio as a retail-participation fade
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. On the bar with dow==0: wkVol = mean volume of this Sat+Sun bars; wdVol = mean volume of the preceding 5 weekday bars. w = close[i]/close[prior Friday bar]-1. If wkVol/wdVol >= ratio and w > 0 -> -1; if wkVol/wdVol >= ratio and w < 0 -> +1; else 0.
rationale: Weekend volume normally runs well below weekday volume; a weekend that trades heavier than the week is retail-driven and such crowd-led moves have faded.
source: Kaiko weekend volume reports; Coinbase retail vs institutional flow notes 2021

name: Weekly options expiry (Friday 08:00 UTC) breakout
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=6. On Friday bars (dow==5) with expiryHour <= hour < expiryHour+windowHours: hi/lo = donchian(lookback, i-1). If close[i] > hi -> +1; if close[i] < lo -> -1; else 0. No re-entry while held.
rationale: Deribit weekly expiries at 08:00 UTC Friday remove that week's dealer hedging; the hours after expiry are when a pinned price is free to move.
source: Deribit expiry schedule; SqueezeMetrics/Deribit Insights dealer-gamma notes

name: Hourly trend only during US hours
rule: dow(k)=(floor(time[k]/86400)+4)%7 (0=Sun..6=Sat), hour(k)=floor(time[k]/3600)%24, all UTC, time = bar open. Signal mode. Position = 1 iff ema(close,9) > ema(close,50) AND dow in 1..5 AND startHour <= hour < endHour; else 0.
rationale: Tests whether the trend premium in crypto is concentrated in the US session, when ETF, CME and equity-correlated flow is active, rather than spread evenly across the 24h day.
source: Hoang & Baur 2021; Dyhrberg et al 2018 intraday Bitcoin; practitioner 'trade the US session' rule

name: Keltner channel breakout (EMA20 +/- 2 ATR10)
rule: Signal mode. upper = ema(close,20) + mult*atr(10). Enter long when close[i] > upper. Exit (0) when close[i] < ema(close,20). Hold otherwise.
rationale: A close beyond two ATRs above the mean is a volatility-defined breakout that adapts to each coin's regime; Keltner breakouts are a standard trend-entry people ask about and have not been tested here.
source: Keltner 1960 'How to Make Money in Commodities'; Chester Keltner channel as popularised by Linda Raschke

name: NR7 compression then next-day breakout (Crabel)
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. range[k]=high[k]-low[k]. NR7 at bar i-1 iff range[i-1] is the smallest of range[i-7..i-1]. If NR7 at i-1 and close[i] > high[i-1] -> +1; if NR7 at i-1 and close[i] < low[i-1] -> -1; else 0.
rationale: Toby Crabel's narrowest-range-of-seven marks energy compression; the first expansion out of it has historically continued for a few bars across markets.
source: Crabel 1990 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns and Opening Range Breakout'

name: Inside-day NR4 (ID/NR4) breakout (Crabel)
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. ID/NR4 at bar i-1 iff high[i-1]<high[i-2] and low[i-1]>low[i-2] and range[i-1] is the smallest of range[i-4..i-1]. If ID/NR4 at i-1 and close[i] > high[i-1] -> +1; if close[i] < low[i-1] -> -1; else 0.
rationale: An inside day that is also the narrowest of four is the tightest short-term compression pattern Crabel found; its breakouts had the best follow-through in his data.
source: Crabel 1990; Linda Raschke & Connors 1995 'Street Smarts' (ID/NR4)

name: Hourly wide-range bar closing at its extreme: continuation
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=6. rng=high[i]-low[i]; wide = rng >= mult*atr(24,i-1). pos=(close[i]-low[i])/rng. If wide and pos >= 1-closePos -> +1; if wide and pos <= closePos -> -1; else 0. No re-entry while held.
rationale: A bar three times the average range that closes at its extreme shows one-sided initiative flow with no absorption; in a market with liquidation cascades this flow has tended to continue for hours.
source: Wide-range-bar continuation (Raschke); mirrors the tested weekly WRB on an hourly scale

name: Parkinson-vol regime switch on hourly bars: breakout when quiet, fade when loud
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=6. pv = sqrt(mean over last 24 bars of ln(high/low)^2) (Parkinson). pct = rank of pv among its own last 720 values. If pct <= 0.2 and close[i] > donchian(24,i-1).upper -> +1; if pct <= 0.2 and close[i] < donchian(24,i-1).lower -> -1. If pct >= 0.8: r=close[i]/close[i-4]-1; if r >= fadeRet -> -1; if r <= -fadeRet -> +1. Else 0.
rationale: Range-based volatility is a far more efficient estimator than close-to-close; using it to decide whether the hour is in a compression or an exhaustion regime separates breakouts from blow-offs.
source: Parkinson 1980 J. Business; regime-conditional trading literature (Kaufman efficiency / volatility regimes)

name: Three-day range compression then breakout
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. compressed iff range[i-1],range[i-2],range[i-3] are all <= frac*atr(20,i-4). hi=max(high[i-3..i-1]), lo=min(low[i-3..i-1]). If compressed and close[i] > hi -> +1; if compressed and close[i] < lo -> -1; else 0.
rationale: Three consecutive sub-normal ranges mean three days of balance; the break of that three-day box is the smallest multi-day breakout that still carries information, a third variant of the Crabel family.
source: Crabel 1990; Nison range-contraction patterns

name: Dominance extreme mean-reversion: rotate into alts after BTC has outrun them
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. domSpread = BTC 60-day return minus EW-alt 60-day return. If domSpread >= spread (BTC outran alts by 20pp) and not already in an alt leg: hold EW alts for the next 30 days (hold weights fixed across rebalances until 30 days elapse). Otherwise hold BTCUSDT only (weight 1). [prereg fix: the alt leg ends at the first weekly rebalance where t - entryT >= 30*86400 s; EW-alt 60-day return = mean of each alt's own 60-day return over alts with >= 61 bars.]
rationale: Capital rotates from BTC into alts after BTC-led legs ('alt season' follows BTC dominance peaks); the tested dominance strategies follow dominance momentum, this tests the contrarian turn.
source: TradingView BTC.D altseason conventions; Blockchain Center 'Altcoin Season Index' methodology

name: Dispersion-conditioned momentum: pick winners only when coins disagree
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. disp = cross-sectional std of 7-day returns over all coins with history. pct = rank of disp among its own last dispHist weekly values (store in ctx.state). If pct >= 0.8: hold top 3 coins by 7-day return EW. Else hold BTCUSDT only. [prereg fix: dispHist 180 -> 52 weekly values (180 weeks would burn ~3.5 years of a ~7-year sample as warm-up); until 52 values are stored, hold BTCUSDT only. Dispersion uses coins with >= 8 bars.]
rationale: Cross-sectional momentum profits scale with return dispersion (Stivers & Sun): when every coin moves together there is nothing to pick, when they diverge the leaders have idiosyncratic information.
source: Stivers & Sun 2010 JFQA 'Cross-sectional return dispersion and time variation in value and momentum premiums'

name: Alt-beta regime: alts only when they amplify BTC
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. beta = OLS slope of EW-alt daily returns on BTC daily returns over the last 60 days. Keep ctx.state.mode: set mode='alts' when beta >= 1.3, 'btc' when beta <= 1.0, unchanged between. mode alts: hold top 5 alts by 20-day return EW; mode btc: BTCUSDT weight 1.
rationale: Alts carry high beta to BTC only in risk-on phases; when their beta compresses toward 1 the speculative bid has left and BTC alone keeps the market return at lower variance.
source: Bianchi & Babiak 2022 'A factor model for cryptocurrency returns' (beta time variation); Liu-Tsyvinski-Wu 2022 crypto factors

name: Large-cap vs mid-cap crypto rotation by relative momentum
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. Rank coins by 30-day mean dollar volume (close*volume). Large = top 6, Mid = bottom 6 of coins with history. mom(group) = mean 30-day return of its members. Hold the group with the higher mom, EW across its 6 members. [prereg fix: needs >= 12 coins with >= 31 bars, else hold BTCUSDT only; with >= 12 coins Large and Mid never overlap.]
rationale: Liquidity tiers of crypto trend in waves (money flows from majors to smaller caps and back); rotating between size buckets by their relative momentum captures the wave rather than a static size premium.
source: Liu, Tsyvinski & Wu 2022 'Common risk factors in cryptocurrency' (size factor); sector-rotation momentum (Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999)

name: Short-term volume surge with positive return (continuation)
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. For each coin: vr = mean volume over last 5 days / mean volume over last 60 days; r5 = 5-day return. Candidates = coins with vr >= 2.0 and r5 > 0. Hold up to 3 candidates with highest vr, EW; if none, hold cash.
rationale: A doubling of turnover with rising price marks attention arriving at a coin; attention-driven inflows in crypto have continued for a week or more before fading.
source: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin 2001 'High-volume return premium'; Barber & Odean attention effects

name: Momentum acceleration (recent momentum minus scaled longer momentum)
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. score = (7-day return) - (28-day return)/4. Hold top 3 coins by score EW.
rationale: Accelerating price (recent return beating its longer-run pace) captures the convex phase of a trend while plain momentum averages in the stale part; shown to beat level momentum in equities.
source: Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer & Swaminathan 2005 / Chen & Yu 2014 'Acceleration and momentum' ; Ardila et al 2015 on price acceleration

name: Negative-skewness premium: avoid positively skewed (lottery-like) coins
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Monthly. skew = sample skewness of daily returns over 90 days. Hold the 5 coins with the most negative skew, EW.
rationale: Investors overpay for right-skewed payoffs, so the most lottery-like coins should earn less and the negatively skewed earn a premium; the single-coin hourly skew test is a different horizon.
source: Bali, Cakici & Whitelaw 2011 'Maxing out'; Boyer, Mitton & Vorkink 2010 'Expected idiosyncratic skewness'

name: Relative-strength breakout versus BTC: alts making a 50-day high in their BTC ratio
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. For each alt: ratio series = alt close / BTC close. Candidate if today's ratio is the highest of the last 50 days. Hold up to 5 candidates (highest 50-day ratio return first) EW; if none, hold BTCUSDT.
rationale: Pricing alts in BTC strips out the market move; a coin breaking out against BTC is gaining share of the market's capital, a relative-strength signal pro desks watch and no test here uses.
source: Relative strength (Levy 1967); crypto-native BTC-pair charting convention

name: Sector rotation: PoW payment coins vs smart-contract/DeFi coins
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. momPow = mean 30-day return of pow members; momSc = mean 30-day return of sc members (members lacking history are skipped). Hold the sector with the higher mom, EW across its members.
rationale: Crypto narratives rotate by sector (old-chain payment coins versus smart-contract/DeFi); sector momentum, distinct from single-coin momentum, has been profitable in equities and is untested here.
source: Moskowitz & Grinblatt 1999 'Do industries explain momentum?'; Messari sector taxonomy

name: Volume-share dominance: BTC's share of market turnover rising = risk-off
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. share(d) = BTC dollar volume / sum of dollar volume of all coins on day d. If mean share over last 7 days > mean share over last 60 days: hold BTCUSDT only. Else hold top 5 alts by 20-day return EW.
rationale: Turnover migrating toward BTC means traders are retreating to the most liquid asset (de-risking); the tested dominance filters use price ratios, this one uses where the volume actually goes.
source: Kaiko 'BTC volume dominance' research; flight-to-liquidity literature (Longstaff 2004)

name: Narrow leadership: BTC at a 50-day high while alt breadth is weak
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. btcHigh = BTC close is the highest close of the last 50 days. breadth = fraction of alts with close > sma(close,50). If btcHigh and breadth < 0.4: hold BTCUSDT only. Else if breadth >= 0.4: hold top 5 alts by 20-day return EW. Else hold cash.
rationale: A BTC-only advance with most alts below their averages is narrow leadership, usually ETF or macro-driven; chasing alts in that state has been a losing trade, while broad participation is when alt momentum pays.
source: Breadth/leadership analysis (Desmond, Lowry's); Zweig breadth concepts applied to crypto

name: Alt/BTC ratio z-score reversion, long-short
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly, longShort. ratio = EW-alt index (cumulative EW alt daily returns) / BTC close, both rebased; z = (ln ratio today - mean of ln ratio over 60 days)/std over 60 days. If z <= -2: alts +0.5 EW total, BTCUSDT -0.5. If z >= +2: alts -0.5 EW total, BTCUSDT +0.5. Else cash. Position held until |z| < 0.5 then cash. [prereg fix: longShort goes in meta (meta.longShort: true), not params. State machine in ctx.state: flat -> enter the z-side leg when |z| >= 2; keep that leg until |z| < 0.5, then cash; no flip from one leg to the other without passing through cash. Alts = alts with >= 61 bars on day t.]
rationale: The alt/BTC ratio is bounded by rotation between the two sides of one market; a two-sigma stretch has tended to snap back, and a market-neutral construction removes the BTC direction bet entirely.
source: Pairs trading (Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst 2006); BTC.D mean-reversion conventions

name: Idiosyncratic volume shock relative to the market
rule: Portfolio (rank) mode, universe CRYPTO_DAILY, universe[sym] = bars up to rebalance day t; alts = every coin except BTCUSDT with enough history; EW = equal weight. Weekly. For each coin zv = (ln vol today - mean ln vol 30d)/std; market zm = mean zv across coins. idio = zv - zm. Candidates: idio >= 2.0 and 1-day return > 0. Hold up to 3 by idio EW for the week; none -> cash. [prereg fix: removed unused param hold; holding period is the weekly rebalance.]
rationale: A volume shock that is unique to one coin, not a market-wide burst, signals coin-specific news; relative-to-market abnormal volume removes the common liquidation days that make plain volume ratios noisy.
source: Gervais, Kaniel & Mingelgrin 2001; Chordia & Swaminathan 2000 volume and lead-lag

name: Daily Garman-Klass volatility expansion continuation
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=3. gk[k] = 0.5*ln(high/low)^2 - (2ln2-1)*ln(close/open)^2. med = median of gk over k in i-30..i-1. If gk[i] >= mult*med: +1 if close[i] > open[i], -1 if close[i] < open[i]. Else 0. No re-entry while held.
rationale: A daily range twice the recent norm with a directional close is an information event; the hourly realised-vol breakout was tested, the daily OHLC-based version is a different horizon and estimator.
source: Garman & Klass 1980 J. Business; vol-expansion continuation (Connors & Raschke)

name: VIX-level gate on a crypto trend
rule: Signal mode. v = ctx.macro('VIX') (null -> treat as 20). Long iff close[i] > sma(close,50) AND v < 30; else 0.
rationale: Equity volatility above 30 marks global de-risking in which crypto's correlation to stocks spikes toward one; the tested VIX rules used shocks and term structure, the plain level gate is the one retail actually asks about.
source: Cboe VIX; Iyer 2022 IMF 'Cryptic connections' (crypto-equity correlation in stress)

name: Trend-strength regime by R-squared of the log-price fit: trend-follow when linear, fade when not
rule: Signal mode. Fit OLS of ln(close) on bar index over the last 90 bars; r2 = R-squared, slope sign s. If r2 >= 0.7: long iff s > 0 and close[i] > sma(close,50), else 0. If r2 <= 0.3: long when rsi(2) < 10, hold until rsi(2) > 60, else 0. Between thresholds keep prior position.
rationale: A high R-squared log-price fit means the market is trending cleanly and trend rules should work; a low fit means noise around a level, where short-term reversion rules work. Switching by fit quality is a halving-free regime filter.
source: Trend-quality R-squared (Kaufman 'Trading Systems and Methods'); Connors RSI2 for the range regime

name: Hurst-exponent regime switch (persistence vs anti-persistence)
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=5. H = rescaled-range Hurst estimate over the last 120 daily log returns (R/S on the full window and halves, slope of log(R/S) vs log(n)). r = close[i]/close[i-20]-1. If H >= 0.55: position = sign(r). If H <= 0.45: position = -sign(r). Else 0. No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: R/S estimate: for n in {30, 60, 120} split the last 120 log returns into 120/n non-overlapping chunks, R/S per chunk = (max-min of cumulative mean-adjusted sum)/population std, average per n; H = OLS slope of ln(avg R/S) on ln(n). A chunk with std 0 returns 0 for the bar.]
rationale: The Hurst exponent measures whether returns persist or revert; crypto has shown H well above 0.5 in trending phases and below in ranging ones, so conditioning the sign of a momentum bet on H is a direct test of that claim.
source: Hurst 1951; Bariviera 2017 'The inefficiency of Bitcoin revisited' (Hurst time variation); Urquhart 2016

name: Turnover-participation filter on a trend
rule: Signal mode. dv = close*volume. part = mean dv over last 20 days > median dv over last 100 days. Long iff close[i] > sma(close,50) AND part; else 0.
rationale: Trends that run on rising participation are fed by new money; the same price trend on drying volume is distribution. A volume-regime filter, unlike the tested volume-confirmed re-entry, gates the whole holding period.
source: Wyckoff volume principles; Lee & Swaminathan 2000 'Price momentum and trading volume'

name: Realised-price proxy: 90-day VWAP as cost basis
rule: Signal mode. vwap = sum(close*volume over last 90 bars)/sum(volume). Long iff close[i] > vwap AND vwap > vwap at bar i-10 (rising cost basis); else 0.
rationale: On-chain 'realised price' (average cost basis of holders) is the most cited crypto bull/bear line; a volume-weighted 90-day price is the exchange-data proxy for it and nobody has tested the proxy here.
source: Glassnode realised price / MVRV; Coin Metrics 'Realized Cap' 2018

name: Long-term-holder cost-basis proxy: 155-day VWAP reclaim
rule: Signal mode. vwap = sum(close*volume over last 155 bars)/sum(volume). Enter long when close[i] > vwap*(1+band). Exit (0) when close[i] < vwap*(1-band). Hold otherwise.
rationale: 155 days is the on-chain threshold separating long-term from short-term holders; price reclaiming the long-term holders' cost basis with a hysteresis band is the second variant of the realised-price family.
source: Glassnode LTH/STH 155-day definition; Checkmate 2021 LTH cost-basis notes

name: Monthly market structure: higher high and higher low on completed monthly bars
rule: Signal mode. M = ctx.resample(bars,'1M') restricted to complete bars. Need >= 3 complete months. Long iff M[-1].high > M[-2].high AND M[-1].low > M[-2].low. Exit (0) when M[-1].low < M[-2].low. Otherwise keep prior position. Evaluated every daily bar using only complete months.
rationale: Monthly swing structure is the slowest market-structure filter practitioners use; a break of the prior month's low has marked every major crypto top, while hourly fractal structure was too noisy in the tested version.
source: Dow Theory trend definition; ICT/SMC monthly structure conventions

name: Time-under-water regime: cash after 60 days without a 100-day high
rule: Signal mode. daysSince = bars since close last equalled the max close of the trailing 100 bars. If daysSince > 60: 0 (bear). Re-enter long when close[i] is a new 50-day high. Otherwise keep prior position (start long once history >= 100 bars and daysSince <= 60).
rationale: Time, not depth, separates a correction from a bear market: markets that fail to print a new high for two months have usually entered distribution; the duration-based regime is untested here.
source: Duration-of-drawdown regime (Faber 2007 style timing); Burggraf & Rudolf 2020 crypto drawdown duration

name: Relative volume by hour-of-day with a 24h breakout
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=12. base = mean volume of the same hour-of-day over the last 20 days (bars i-24, i-48, ..., i-480). rvol = volume[i]/base. If rvol >= 3 and close[i] > donchian(24,i-1).upper -> +1; if rvol >= 3 and close[i] < donchian(24,i-1).lower -> -1; else 0.
rationale: Crypto volume has a strong intraday seasonal, so raw volume ratios flag the US open every day; relative volume against the same hour removes the seasonal and isolates genuine participation surges at breakouts.
source: RVOL as used in day-trading literature (Bulkowski; Warrior Trading); Admati & Pfleiderer 1988 intraday volume patterns

name: Up-volume to down-volume ratio (volume flow) over 20 days
rule: Signal mode, longShort. up = sum volume on days with close>prev close over last 20; down = sum volume on days with close<prev close. ratio = up/down. Long iff ratio >= 1.5; short iff ratio <= 0.67; else 0. Re-evaluated every bar.
rationale: Volume on up days versus down days measures who is aggressive, buyers or sellers, independent of the net price change; it is the core of the Arms Index and of accumulation/distribution analysis and is untested here.
source: Arms 1989 'The Arms Index (TRIN)'; Chaikin accumulation/distribution

name: Liquidity-improvement momentum: Amihud illiquidity falling
rule: Signal mode, holdBars=10. amihud = mean over last 20 days of |ret|/(close*volume). za = (ln amihud - mean ln amihud over last 120 days)/std. Enter long iff za <= -1.0 AND close[i] > sma(close,50). No re-entry while held.
rationale: A coin whose price impact per dollar is falling is attracting market makers and flow ahead of price; liquidity shocks predict returns in equities (Amihud) and in crypto the liquidity premium is far larger.
source: Amihud 2002 J. Financial Markets; Brauneis & Mestel 2018 crypto liquidity

name: Orderly deleveraging: OI down sharply while price holds
rule: oi(k)=ctx.openInterest(k). Signal mode, holdBars=10. d = oi(i)/oi(i-7)-1; r = close[i]/close[i-7]-1. Enter long iff d <= -0.15 AND r >= -0.05. No re-entry while held. [prereg fix: OI is used coin-denominated, oic(k)=ctx.openInterest(k)/close[k]; every oi(...) above means oic(...). If any needed OI value is null the bar returns 0 (no signal), and nulls are never pushed into a window or treated as 0.]
rationale: Leverage leaving the market without a price crash means positions were closed voluntarily, not liquidated; the tested flush-bounce needs a crash, this is the calm reset, which leaves a cleaner base for a move up.
source: Glassnode 'OI reset without price capitulation' 2023 notes; Coinglass OI research

name: Stealth breakout: 20-day high on below-median volume
rule: Signal mode, holdBars=10. Enter long iff close[i] > donchian(20,i-1).upper AND volume[i] < median of volume over i-20..i-1. No re-entry while held.
rationale: The opposite claim to volume-confirmed breakouts: a quiet breakout has no crowd positioned in it, so the inevitable late buyers and short covering arrive after entry rather than before; a widely argued rule that deserves a direct test.
source: Contrarian to Weinstein/O'Neil volume confirmation; 'stealth breakout' practitioner literature (Minervini)

name: Hourly return autocorrelation regime: momentum when positive, reversal when negative
rule: Signal mode, longShort, holdBars=1. ac = lag-1 autocorrelation of the last 168 hourly returns. If ac >= 0.05: position = sign(ret[i]). If ac <= -0.05: position = -sign(ret[i]). Else 0. Re-evaluated every bar. [prereg fix: hourly sign(ret[i]) with holdBars 1 flips every hour at 0.10%/side and only measures cost drag; position now = sign (or -sign) of the last 24h return close[i]/close[i-24]-1, holdBars 24, no re-entry while held. ac still = lag-1 autocorrelation of the last 168 hourly returns.]
rationale: Hourly crypto returns alternate between momentum and reversal regimes as liquidity and liquidation activity change; the daily variance-ratio switch was tested, the hourly autocorrelation version is the third persistence-regime variant on a different clock.
source: Lo & MacKinlay 1988; Urquhart 2016 Bitcoin efficiency; Caporale et al 2018 persistence in crypto
